editorial.thesis: A hospitality-and-learning city of about 60,000. Its retail is heavy on cafés, tea & coffee and restaurants & fast food, and thin on pharmacy & health retail and apparel, footwear & jewellery — and 0% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is ahead of Delhi. 19.93 chain outlets per lakh residents against 18.83 in Delhi; 7 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Reliance Trends 4, Chai Sutta Bar 3, Domino's 1.

The mapped economy leans to hotels & stays. Shares of all mapped places: hotels & stays 23.7% (Delhi 4.4%); education 9.6% (Delhi 7.9%); offices 4.6% (Delhi 11.7%); shops & retail 10.0% (Delhi 17.2%). Raw counts would mislead because Delhi is mapped more completely (87,703 places against 668), so we compare mix, not counts.
No large under-served zone. No zone combines a large resident base with retail depth below 60% of the city average; the thin spots are small and scattered.
Retail is more concentrated than in Delhi. 49% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Delhi 47%). The largest core is Pokharkhali · Lala Bazar (351 places).

The widest brand gaps against Delhi. Café Coffee Day 0 outlets vs 145; Domino's 1 outlets vs 140; Apollo Pharmacy 0 outlets vs 108. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 5 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Delhi, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Pokharkhali · Lala Bazar is the only mapped zone, with about 44,000 residents. Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 49% of all commercial places, and Pokharkhali · Lala Bazar alone lists 351.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Pokharkhali · Lala Bazar holds 10 of the 12 tracked chain outlets.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Pokharkhali · Lala Bazar has 42 education places and 14 coaching centres.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. There is no large amber area. The blue cores include Pokharkhali · Lala Bazar.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (87,703 places in Delhi against 668 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Delhi; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Delhi, Almora's mapped places over-index on hotels & stays (23.7% vs 4.4%), education (9.6% vs 7.9%), food & beverage (9.6% vs 8.0%) and under-index on offices (4.6% vs 11.7%), shops & retail (10.0% vs 17.2%), banks & finance (5.5% vs 7.9%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 12 outlets of 7 tracked national brands within 5 km — 19.93 per lakh residents against Delhi's 18.83 (1289 outlets of 45 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Delhi are Café Coffee Day (0 vs 145); Domino's (1 vs 140); Apollo Pharmacy (0 vs 108). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Delhi's, so low means thin by Delhi's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 5 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Almora's age mix against Delhi: children (0–14) 25.8% vs 23.1%, 15–24 19.5% vs 20.4%, working age 42.4% vs 49.7%, 60+ 12.3% vs 6.8%. Under-25s are 45% of residents.

zones.263601: Reasonably supplied: 351 places for about 44,000 residents (index 100), 10 chain outlets.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 6.9% of mapped places against 5.7% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 1 (Delhi 140).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 3.6% of mapped places against 2.1% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Chai Sutta Bar 3 (Delhi 0).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.6% of mapped places against 0.7% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 1 (Delhi 29). No mapped outlet in either city: Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 2.1% of mapped places against 2.2% in Delhi, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Vishal Mega Mart 1 (Delhi 11). No mapped outlet in either city: Star Bazaar.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 0.5% of mapped places against 1.2% in Delhi — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: MedPlus, Wellness Forever, Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 3.7% of mapped places against 7.0% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Trends 4 (Delhi 22), Pantaloons 1 (Delhi 8), Bata 1 (Delhi 66).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 5.5% of mapped places against 7.9% in Delhi — below its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 2.1% of mapped places against 2.7% in Delhi — below its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 2.1% of mapped places against 3.9% in Delhi — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
